results.fact: Whether trailhead parking requires a fee/pass
results.evidence: Still open on retry. The live row still disagrees: access.passRequired says 'Recreation pass' and `permit` mentions a Northwest Forest Pass, while access.parking_pass/notes say the crag's unofficial pullout is not a fee site. The crag's area description gives only the pullout location (uphill of the double hairpin ~1.4 mi from US-2), with nothing about a pass; the nearby Wellington Trailhead is the fee site. results.fact: Permit field names the Wild Sky Wilderness
results.evidence: A new source settles part of it: querying the Forest Service's own wilderness-boundary map service at the crag coordinate (47.75586, -121.11626) returns no wilderness, no part of the Wild Sky Wilderness lies within 4 km, and the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness boundary lies only ~150-200 m away. So the Wild Sky name is wrong, but because the crag pin is approximate and the HMJ boundary is that close, whether the crag is inside HMJ (self-issue permit applies) or just outside it (no permit) cannot be settled. Rewriting `permit` needs that answer, so nothing is patched.

results.fact: 'Rampart Lakes' waypoint on the Hibox route
results.evidence: The fact is settled but the fix is out of scope. The Rachel Lake trail runs 3.5 mi to Rachel Lake, and Rampart Lakes lie beyond it, reached by climbing half a mile to Rampart Ridge and then going about a mile left; the row's own beta, approach and pitch_detail have the Hibox boot path leave the trail at ~2 mi, below Rachel Lake, heading northeast. The 'Rampart Lakes' Junction pin (no elev, no distMi, no note) therefore is not on this route. The only correct fix is removing the pin, which is pin work outside this patch scope; renaming it would not help because it sits at the real Rampart Lakes. Flagged for the pin pass.

Still real in the live row: itinerary 5.7 + 9.2 = 14.9 mi against the approach's '~16.8-mile (27 km) round-trip'. A club route profile (search summary; the page is behind a bot wall) gives trailhead to camp ~5.7 mi / 4,000 ft and camp to summit ~1.5 mi / 1,500 ft, and hike pages give 11.7-12 mi round trip to Sahale Glacier Camp. A round-trip figure for Horseshoe would have to be added up from those legs, which is a computed value, and no source states a car-to-car total. Left open.

Still real: the day-2 schedule returns to camp at 1:00 PM after a 4:00 AM start, then adds the 5.7 mi / 4,000 ft descent, which cannot fit the 10 h in days[1].hours, summitTimeHrs and sectionBreakdown[1]. The only new figure is a club profile's 4-6 h for camp to summit (one way or round trip is not clear from the summary) and 4-6 h trailhead to camp; nothing states the day's total, and the Cascades trip-report forum page would not load. Whether the hours or the schedule is wrong stays unsettled.

The park's own trail page confirms the East Bank trail leaves Ross Lake for Lightning Creek at mile 16 from SR-20 (31 mi to Hozomeen), and puts the Hozomeen Lake junction about 3 mi north of Willow Lake, so Willow Lake is roughly mile 25-26 from SR-20, not '~mile 20' as its note says; the distMi values 11 and 15 fit neither origin. The Willow Lake note and both distMi need rewriting, but no source states Willow Lake's mileage directly (only derivable by subtraction, which is not allowed), and the pin positions themselves look off-route, which is out of scope. Left for the pin pass.
Already consistent: the live row now has dist_km 9.7 (about 6 mi one way), which agrees with the itinerary's ~12 mi round trip and the approach's ~19 km round trip.

results.fact: Total gain: gain_ft vs itinerary gain
results.evidence: Already consistent: gain_ft and loss_ft are now both 6300, matching the itinerary's day totals (6,300 up; 1,200 + 5,100 down) and the totalNote; the approach's 'roughly 6,400+ ft' is a rounded estimate within about 100 ft.

results.fact: Total elevation gain vs. loss for a car-to-car round trip
results.evidence: Still real: gain_ft 6266 (the net elevation range) and loss_ft 545 (camp to saddle only). Published car-to-car figures from Skyline II cluster near 9,000-9,600 ft but do not agree: one two-day report gives 24 mi and 9,600 ft; a club route profile gives 9,080 ft; a single-push party measured 44 km and 2,800 m (~9,200 ft) but that included three extra peaks. No two sources state the same figure for this route alone, so neither column is changed.
